name: What is the difference between a vanishing edge (infinity) pool and a perimeter overflow pool?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a vanishing edge (infinity) pool and a perimeter overflow pool?

acceptedAnswer.text: A vanishing edge, or infinity pool, creates the illusion that one or more edges of the pool merge with the horizon or a larger body of water, achieved by the water flowing over the edge into a catch basin below. A perimeter overflow pool, however, has water flowing over all four sides (or more) into a hidden gutter system, creating a mirror-like surface effect. Vanishing edge pools emphasize a dramatic view, while perimeter overflow pools offer a sleek, architectural statement with a perpetually smooth water surface. Both are complex to design and construct, requiring specialized engineering.
acceptedAnswer.description: A vanishing edge pool has water flowing over one or more sides into a lower basin, creating an 'infinity' illusion. A perimeter overflow pool has water flowing over all edges into a hidden gutter, creating a mirror-like surface.
